root_idea.summary: The root denotes inclination, deflection, or turning aside from a line or course.
root_idea.development: From the basic idea of deviation or lateral inclination, the lexical range extends to turning away, oblique winds, the shoulder as a lateral junction, ailments causing lameness, and related figurative or occupational uses.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized singular citation form مَنْكِب, whose plural occurs in the Quran.
Displayed under the normalized active-participle citation form نَاكِب.

senses.definition: A side, lateral region, or elevated part of the earth.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic plural construction مَنَاكِبِهَا, the earth is described through the metaphor of shoulders; the expression has also been interpreted as its routes or mountains.

senses.definition: Deviating or turning away from the straight path.
senses.usage_conditions: An active participle of نَكَبَ عَنْ; in the Quranic expression عَنِ الصِّرَاطِ لَنَاكِبُونَ, it denotes moral or religious deviation from the straight course.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To turn aside or away from a person, thing, road, or course; to avoid, separate oneself from, or go off at a distance.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used with عن and related directional constructions; the meaning includes physical departure and deviation from a course.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of the wind: to blow obliquely, between the directions of two cardinal winds.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A meteorological use describing a wind that does not follow a cardinal direction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To throw, cast, or fling; to throw someone down.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The transitive construction نَكَبَ بِهِ may specify throwing someone onto the ground.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of fortune or circumstance: to overcome, afflict, or smite someone with a disaster or calamity; to be afflicted by such fortune.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Includes the active and passive expressions describing a person struck by misfortune.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To empty or pour out the contents of a vessel or quiver by throwing down or inverting it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The vessel usage is especially applied to non-fluid contents such as dust; with a quiver, it may involve scattering the arrows.

other_classical_meanings.definition: For stones to hit, wound, or make bleed the foot, hoof, nail, or camel’s foot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The injury is conventionally associated with being struck by stones while walking.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To suffer a shoulder-joint ailment that causes halting; of a man, to have pain in the shoulder joint.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The animal usage is specifically applied to camels and their shoulder or shoulder-blade.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An intendant, superintendent, or assistant over a people; in an administrative hierarchy, a chief or assistant of the ʿurafāʾ.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The title is metaphorically related to the shoulder as a supporting part.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To remove, put aside, or put out of the way a person or thing.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The causative Form II construction may be transitive or intransitive in the cited usage.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To throw a bow or quiver over the shoulder; to shoulder it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A Form V construction for carrying an object on the shoulder.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To lean upon a bow or staff.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate Form V construction with على.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An inclination or deflection in a thing, or something resembling such an inclination.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term can describe a physical slant or deviation from a line.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A stone-inflicted injury to the foot causing pain or bleeding.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This concrete sense is distinct from the figurative sense of misfortune.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A misfortune, evil accident, disaster, affliction, or calamity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension from being struck or injured.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A heap of corn or grain that has not been measured or weighed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical agricultural or commercial term, synonymous with صُبْرَةٌ in the cited evidence.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The circuit or circumference of a hoof or a camel’s foot.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An anatomical term for the outer circuit of the foot or hoof.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who deviates greatly from the right course of action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An adjectival description of pronounced moral or behavioral deviation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An oblique wind blowing between two cardinal directions.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may designate one of the four winds between the cardinal winds, with different traditional names and qualities according to direction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A camel affected by disease in the shoulder joint or shoulder blade, or one that walks as though leaning to one side.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The description combines the shoulder ailment with its characteristic one-sided gait.

other_classical_meanings.definition: An inclining pulley.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical description of a pulley set at an angle.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Overpowering or oppressive; unjust or tyrannical.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative adjectival use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a proverbial expression, fortune is prone to repeated disasters and does not remain in one state.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional statement portraying fortune as repeatedly deviating from a stable course.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A man who has no bow with him.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal adjective use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The shoulder, especially the junction of the upper arm and shoulder blade.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural مَنَاكِبُ can denote the two shoulders or the shoulder joints collectively.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To shake the shoulders as an expression of rejoicing or happiness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An idiomatic figurative construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In a prayer-related expression, easy or pliant shoulders, interpreted as keeping still or making room for someone entering the row.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional expression whose interpretation concerns conduct and spacing in prayer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The name of certain stars identified with the shoulder of a constellation, including a star in Pegasus and a bright star in Orion.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An astronomical naming use derived from the shoulder metaphor.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The secondary feathers of a bird’s wing, immediately after the primary feathers.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term is reported as a plural without a securely attested singular; these feathers were also used in feathering arrows.

other_classical_meanings.definition: One who deviates greatly from the right course of action.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized derived noun for pronounced deviation.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Having the foot wounded, struck, or made to bleed by stones.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial description of stone injury.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Overcome or afflicted by fortune, especially through an evil accident or disaster.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative passive-participial use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A road that deviates from the right course or direction.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun describing a crooked or deflected route.

cautions: The Quranic مَنَاكِبِهَا is securely associated with مَنْكِب, but the reported interpretations vary between the earth’s sides or elevated regions, its roads, and its mountains.
The Quranic نَاكِبُونَ is presented under the normalized active-participle citation form نَاكِب rather than the inflected plural surface form.
